style: Athletic, direct side under Carlos Queiroz emphasizing defensive structure and rapid counter-attacks. Pace and power on the flanks through Semenyo and Williams, with Partey providing control in midfield; can struggle for creativity in tight games.
recent_form: Qualified for the finals via CAF, with Mohammed Kudus's goal against Comoros sealing the spot. Notably, Kudus was left out of the final World Cup squad in a major selection talking point.

key_players.name: Antoine Semenyo
key_players.note: Ghana's most exciting player; lit up the Premier League with Bournemouth before a January move and is a guaranteed starter.

key_players.name: Thomas Partey
key_players.note: Villarreal midfielder bringing experience and control; the metronome of the side despite limited club minutes.

key_players.name: Inaki Williams
key_players.note: Athletic Bilbao forward with pace to stretch defences; a certainty in the attack.

key_players.name: Jordan Ayew
key_players.note: Captains the Black Stars; experienced finisher with a strong international scoring record.

key_players.name: Mohammed Salisu
key_players.note: Composed defender anchoring the back line for Queiroz's structured setup.

historical_news: Qualified for the 2026 World Cup via CAF, with Mohammed Kudus's goal v Comoros sealing the berth.
Marquee midfielder Mohammed Kudus controversially omitted from the final World Cup squad.
Carlos Queiroz named the official 26-man squad in late May 2026.
Antoine Semenyo lifted the Carabao Cup in March after a January transfer, headlining his breakout season.
Drawn into Group F alongside Croatia, Egypt and Panama.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Mixed Ghanaian sentiment: excitement over Semenyo's form and Partey's experience offset by debate over Kudus's exclusion and a tough group; cautious optimism about reaching the knockouts.
